title: Ramp Controller: Phase-slit Prefill/Decode Congestion Policy
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Under mixed workloads (short chat requests + long generation), the existing phase-splitting schedulers oscillate between prioritizing throughput and low percentile latency. When bursty prefill traffic hits a node with limited KV cache locality, long decode streams get starved and kernel selection paths degrade (fallback to slower kernels due to cold caches).

Proposal: Implement a "ramp controller" that smooths phase-slit allocations across the prefill->decode transition. The controller uses short-term telemetry (per-tenant token backlog, kernel probe latency, recent attention memory pressure) to create a scored allocation vector that: (1) prevents decode starvation by reserving minimal decode headroom proportional to long-run tail risk, (2) opportunistically opens extra prefill capacity when kernel probes indicate fast paths are available, and (3) gracefully rebalances when attention RAM pressure or kernel latency rises.

Key behaviors: reserve-decode-minimum: a tunable floor fraction of active slots kept for decode; adaptive-opening: a multiplicative ramp-up that increases prefill split when kernel probes show <X% slower kernel selection; attention-pressure-shed: when GPU attention memory nearing threshold, temporarily throttle prefill phases and trigger KV cache warming for top-tenants.

Why different: instead of hard phase-splits or purely latency-weighted heuristics, the ramp controller intervenes with short-window probes and multiplicative ramps to reduce oscillation and keep both p50/p95 within targets while improving aggregate throughput. The design explicitly ties kernel selection signals (probe latency, selected-kernel histogram) and attention memory telemetry into scheduling decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Controller is enabled behind a runtime flag and defaults to off

Under mixed synthetic workload (50% short-chat 5-15 tokens, 50% long-gen 200-800 tokens) p95 tail for long-gen should improve or remain within 10% of baseline while aggregate token throughput increases >=5%
No regressions in p50 for short-chat (<=5% degradation) across 10k request sample
Kernel-probe-based fast-path usage increases for prefill when the controller opens capacity (measured via kernel selection histogram)
Unit and integration tests for core controller logic and attention-pressure shedding present
Documentation with config knobs and recommended defaults added to runtime docs
design_notes: Telemetry inputs: per-tenant backlog, recent kernel probe latencies (median+90th), attention memory free bytes, KV cache hit rate for top-5 tenants
Decision cadence: controller runs every 50ms window and computes multipliers applied to phase split allocations
Ramp math: multiplicative ramp with upper bound 3x and lower bound 0.5x on prefill allocation; decode floor configurable as fraction (default 0.12)
Kernel selection integration: if probe 90th percentile latency > threshold, favor decode by reducing prefill multiplier
Isolation: controller respects tenant credits and hard SLO reservations (dedicated tiers) — does not reduce reserved capacity
Fallback: on telemetry failure, controller reverts to current deterministic phase-slit policy
implementation_plan: Add kernel probe exporter: lightweight probe that runs <1% of requests, aggregates selection latency and candidate kernel tags
Implement ramp-controller module with pluggable telemetry adapters
Wire controller outputs into phase allocator and ensure atomic update path with metrics emitted
E2E tests using load-generator harness with mixed request shapes; include attention-pressure fault injection (fake low memory) to validate shedding
Canary rollout to staging, then low-traffic region with feature-flagged enablement for 48h, monitor dashboards and alert-thresholds
Roll forward to 25% traffic, then 100% if metrics within acceptance criteria
test_plan: Unit tests for ramp math, clamp behavior, and probe timeout handling
Integration tests: emulator with kernel-selection shim to simulate fast/slow kernels
Load tests: synthetic mixed workload scenarios comparing baseline scheduler vs ramp controller
Chaos tests: drop kernel-probe telemetry and simulate KV cache cold start to confirm graceful fallback
Regression suite: ensure no increased OOM/GC signals when attention-pressure shedding engages
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Oscillation if controller reacts too aggressively -> Mitigation: add dampening and minimum hold windows (200ms)
Risk: Telemetry noise causes misallocation for small tenants -> Mitigation: per-tenant smoothing + hysteresis and minimum sample counts
Risk: Increased engineering complexity and maintenance -> Mitigation: keep controller opt-in feature-flag and implement clear observability
Risk: Interaction with autoscaler could produce capacity thrash -> Mitigation: expose controller signals as advisory to autoscaler and rate-limit scale decisions
